title: Lesson 34 - By the Time I Got There

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: By the time I got there, all twelve review copies were already on the wall. For one second, I thought I'd brought the wrong candidate list.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I had the same reaction. I was opening the upstairs rooms when Jules, the morning assistant, offered to help with the board.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What had you done before he started?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Before that, I'd printed the temporary number cards and put your folder on the table. Then I went downstairs to let a class in.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And Jules put up the copies while you were downstairs?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Right. A few minutes later, I came back and saw him finishing the last row. At first, everything looked neat. That's when I realized the old bookshop photo was under number eight, not number three.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: It turned out that he had sorted the copies by file name.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Exactly. He thought the numbers in the file names were our candidate numbers.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That makes sense. Those file names show the scan order. I'd already written the real candidate number on the back of each copy before I left the folder here yesterday.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good. Just as I was about to take everything down, I noticed the numbers on the backs. We can fix the order without guessing.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So the sorting had happened before you noticed the first mismatch.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Yes. Then I stopped Jules before he added any working notes. We checked two copies together, but I waited for you before changing the whole board.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks. Let's turn them over one row at a time and match them to the candidate list.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And let's keep the temporary cards separate from the permission records. I don't want an internal number to look like an approval.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Agreed. In the end, nothing was lost or damaged. We only need to restore the sequence and write a clearer instruction for the next review session.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I'll tell Jules what happened. He was trying to help, and the folder didn't explain the two numbering systems.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I'll add a cover sheet: “Use the number on the back. File names show scan order only.”
